cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Processing & Technology
cards.back: Primary processing converts raw food materials into basic ingredients: milling wheat into flour, pasteurising milk, refining sugar cane, and slaughtering and butchering animals.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Processing & Technology
cards.back: Secondary processing converts primary-processed ingredients into more complex products: making flour into bread, milk into cheese, flour and sugar into biscuits, potatoes into crisps.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Processing & Technology
cards.back: Food additives are substances added to food for a specific purpose: preservatives (extend shelf life), colourants (improve appearance), flavourings (enhance taste), emulsifiers (mix oil and water), stabilisers (maintain texture).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Processing & Technology
cards.back: Additives are given E numbers when approved for use in the EU; some consumers prefer additive-free foods due to health concerns (e.g. hyperactivity linked to some colourants).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Processing & Technology
cards.back: Fortification adds nutrients to food to improve public health: folic acid in flour, vitamins A and D in margarine, calcium in plant milks, iron in breakfast cereals.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Processing & Technology
cards.back: Genetic modification (GM) alters an organism's DNA to produce desired traits: pest-resistant crops, vitamin-enriched rice (Golden Rice), herbicide-tolerant soya. GM food is controversial.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Processing & Technology
cards.back: Food irradiation uses ionising radiation to kill bacteria, insects, and parasites; it extends shelf life but is not widely used in the UK due to consumer concern.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Processing & Technology
cards.back: Extrusion cooking forces food through a shaped opening under high temperature and pressure; used for breakfast cereals, pasta shapes, and snack products.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Processing & Technology
cards.back: Modified atmosphere packaging (MAP) replaces air in food packaging with a gas mixture (typically nitrogen and carbon dioxide) to extend shelf life without preservatives.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Processing & Technology
cards.back: Ultra-processed foods (UPFs) are industrially formulated products with many additives; linked to obesity, heart disease, and other health problems when consumed in excess.

cards.front: What should you know about food preparation & nutrition exam tips — food processing & technology?
cards.back: 1. For Food Processing & Technology questions, show every step of your working clearly — method marks count even if the final answer is wrong 2. Check your answer makes sense in context (estimation, units, reasonableness) 3. Use correct mathematical notation and state formulae before substituting values 4. If a Food Processing & Technology question asks you to 'prove' or 'show', write a logical chain of reasoning with a conclusion line 5. For problem-solving, identify the topic first, then recall the relevant method
Explain the difference between primary and secondary food processing, giving examples. Discuss the role of food additives and evaluate their use in processed foods. (8 marks)
